dovish.title: Labour Market Softening
dovish.summary: Job market is cracking: payrolls went negative, far below forecast.
dovish.reason: Payrolls turned negative and prior months were revised lower, signalling a labour-demand inflection and strengthening the insurance-cut case.

dovish.title: ISM Manufacturing Back in Contraction
dovish.summary: Factories are shrinking again — demand is cooling, not overheating.
dovish.reason: Sub-50 output, new orders and employment point to weaker demand and hiring, while lower prices paid reduces the inflation obstacle to easing.

dovish.title: Consumer and Industrial Chain Under Pressure
dovish.summary: Consumer engine sputtering: biggest US retailer cut guidance.
dovish.reason: Softer retail guidance and industrial orders can transmit through earnings, hiring and consumption, reinforcing the slowdown narrative.

dovish.title: Long-End Now Easing — Passive Tightening Fading
dovish.summary: Long rates have eased 10bp w; passive-tightening argument softening.
dovish.reason: Long-end has eased -12bp w (30Y 5.174% from 5.30%) and 10Y -10bp w (4.650% from 4.75%), softening the term-premium/passive-tightening hawkish counter-narrative. Still rich vs forecast 4.80% but the trend is now dovish.

dovish.title: Equity Rally Confirms Risk-On Before Jackson Hole
dovish.summary: Stocks bounced back into Jackson Hole — risk-on, dovish-friendly tape.
dovish.reason: Thu 2026-08-27: SPY +0.59%, QQQ +1.10%, IWM +0.22% on the day — recovery from Tue levels. VIX -4.34% to 14.55. The market is in a risk-on posture heading into Jackson Hole tonight, consistent with dovish pricing. Sector mix: XLE -1.33% d (oil laggard), XLI -0.64% d, XLF -0.51% d — defensives and bonds outperforming. Drivers stay dovish-tilted.

dovish.title: Oil Crash — Demand-Scare Persists
dovish.summary: WTI down 6.6% w; demand scare not yet reversed.
dovish.reason: WTI recovered slightly to $82 on Thu (+2.0% d) but still down 6.6% w from prior $87 level. The cumulative demand-scare signal persists: ISM 48.7 mfg, payrolls negative, China PMI weak. The shock is not a one-day event — it represents a multi-day repricing. Driver weight reduced from 2.0 to 1.5 as some recovery priced in; dovish bias intact.

dovish.title: VIX Collapses — Calmest Tape in Two Months
dovish.summary: VIX 14.55, down 9% w — markets are pricing benign outcome from Jackson Hole.
dovish.reason: VIX dropped to 14.55 — multi-week low — heading into Jackson Hole, implying the market is pricing a balanced or dovish Fed message. Equivolume to dovish drivers; supports the dovish bias.

hawkish.title: Services PMI Big Beat
hawkish.summary: Services economy is running hot, not slowing.
hawkish.reason: Strong services demand, employment and prices paid point to persistent core-services inflation and raise the hurdle for a cut.

hawkish.title: Tariff Inflation Shock
hawkish.summary: Broad reciprocal tariffs add direct imported inflation while expectations are already elevated.
hawkish.reason: Broad reciprocal tariffs add direct imported inflation while inflation expectations are already elevated. First post-tariff Core PCE (Aug 26) is the test — but BLS 403 / FXStreet article pages JS-rendered so exact actual not retrieved live; carried forward forecast MoM 0.20% YoY 2.80% as the data unverified baseline.

hawkish.title: Hawkish 3-Vote Dissent at July FOMC
hawkish.summary: Three regional Fed presidents wanted a hike at the last meeting — the Committee is split.
hawkish.reason: Re-verified 2026-08-27 11:12Z: the July 29 FOMC vote was 9-3 with Hammack (Cleveland), Kashkari (Minneapolis), and Logan (Dallas) all preferring +25bp hike. This is the highest dissent count in 2026 and signals that a meaningful cluster on the FOMC views current policy as too easy. Confirmed via federalreserve.gov press release.

hawkish.title: Gold's Record Run Continues — Inflation-Hedge Bid
hawkish.summary: GC=F +2.93% w; real-money bid for inflation protection persists even with dovish Fed pricing.
hawkish.reason: Gold futures GC=F hit fresh record 4648.8 (+2.93% w) on 2026-08-27. Spot GLD 421.02 has lagged (-1.6% w) — divergence suggests futures-driven institutional bid rather than retail ETF flow. The signal remains: investors pay for inflation protection even while pricing cuts. Weight reduced 1.5 to 1.0 as GLD actually faded w/w.

hawkish.title: Inflation Expectations De-Anchoring
hawkish.summary: Inflation expectations are drifting above the 3% anchor.
hawkish.reason: Five-year expectations above 3% increase concern that inflation psychology is becoming persistent.

dovish.title: US-Canada Reciprocal Tariffs
dovish.summary: US tariffs hit Canada's export engine first and hardest.
dovish.reason: Canada's dependence on US demand means tariffs can quickly reduce export orders, industrial output and employment.

dovish.title: Household Leverage and Mortgage Sensitivity
dovish.summary: Highly indebted households cannot absorb today's rates.
dovish.reason: High leverage and mortgage renewals make Canadian demand unusually sensitive to elevated rates.

dovish.title: Global Manufacturing Pullback
dovish.summary: Global factory slowdown leads Canadian exports lower.
dovish.reason: Global manufacturing weakness leads Canadian resource and industrial exports by one to two months.

dovish.title: Labour Market Marginal Easing
dovish.summary: Unemployment is creeping up — labour slack is building.
dovish.reason: Higher unemployment and slower wage growth indicate more labour-market slack and less wage inflation pressure.

dovish.title: CAD Drifts Near 1.38 — Rate-Spread Trade Pressures Loonie
dovish.summary: CAD still weak; Sep 2 BoC only 6 days away widens the dovish wedge.
dovish.reason: USDCAD closed 1.3836 on Thu (-0.03% d, -0.44% w) — still hovering near post-hold highs. With Sep 2 BoC only 6 days away and Fed cut-vs-hold debate live, the rate-spread trade remains the cleanest dovish signal for CAD.

dovish.title: Oil Collapsed 6.6% w — CAD Terms of Trade Eroded
dovish.summary: WTI $82 erodes CAD support and the BoC's hawkish buffer.
dovish.reason: Canada's terms-of-trade benefit from oil vanishes when WTI drops from $87 to $82 (-5.8% cumulative). The BoC's prior hawkish buffer (oil $87, XLE +0.85% w) flipped to a dovish signal: USD/CAD stuck near 1.38 and the rate-spread trade widened, materially increasing the cut probability into Sep 2 — only 6 days away.

hawkish.title: Retail Sales Big Beat
hawkish.summary: Consumers are still spending — no collapse in sight.
hawkish.reason: Broad retail growth suggests consumption is not collapsing and gives the BOC room to wait.

hawkish.title: Energy Tailwind Reversed — Marked Neutral
hawkish.summary: WTI dropped from $87 to $82 — energy tailwind has flipped to headwind for CAD.
hawkish.reason: WTI dropped from $87 to $82 (-5.8% from prior Hawkish print), flipping the energy tailwind to a headwind for CAD. Driver kept with reduced weight (0.5) to preserve stable ID and history, marked neutral until Aug 28 GDP Fri print.

hawkish.title: GDP Resilience to Be Tested Friday
hawkish.summary: Friday's GDP print is the make-or-break test before the meeting.
hawkish.reason: This is the hardest domestic release before the meeting; a strong print supports holding, while a contraction would pull decisively dovish.

hawkish.title: US Stickiness Spillover — Fed Path Constrains BoC
hawkish.summary: US services 56.8 + hawkish Fed dissent + 30Y 5.17% — BOC can't lead cuts too aggressively.
hawkish.reason: A BOC cut while the Fed is split (9-3 July dissent) would widen the rate gap, weaken CAD and import US inflation. BoC has to read the Fed path carefully — and the Fed now looks more uncertain than at any point in 2026.

calendar.logic: A higher neutral-rate message pulls hawkish; greater dual-mandate balance pulls dovish. Markets pricing balanced/soft (VIX 14.55).
Initial claims above 240k with continuing claims rising would confirm labour deterioration.
A wider deficit would indicate weaker external demand and pull dovish.

calendar.event: Fed Chair Warsh Speech at Jackson Hole
calendar.logic: Inflation-risk emphasis pulls hawkish; dual-mandate balance pulls dovish. Dominant near-term Fed catalyst.
A downward revision larger than 700k would show labour was already weaker than reported.
Expectations rising again would raise the hurdle for a September cut.
MoM at 0.20% or above supports holding; zero or lower can flip the balance dovish before Sep 2 BoC (only 5 days away).
6 days away — needs Fri GDP + Mon PMI to settle. Oil collapse + USD/CAD 1.3836 + tariff drag = dovish tilt, but a strong GDP Fri can keep the BoC on hold for one more meeting.
A deeper sub-50 reading confirms export-order weakness and pulls the BOC dovish ahead of next-day rate decision.

calendar.event: US Payrolls · First After Sep FOMC
calendar.logic: Payrolls below 100k or a higher unemployment rate would materially strengthen the cut case for Oct/Nov FOMC.
A tariff-driven acceleration to 3.2% or higher could force the FOMC to skip the next cut.

calendar.event: FOMC Decision, SEP and Press Conference (Sep 15-16)
calendar.logic: Final Fed settlement of growth/labour/tariff/PCE. Re-priced distribution after rate-base correction: cut 55% / hold 42% / hike 3% — near-50/50 cut-vs-hold, tilted slightly dovish.
